violations.why: Timer_B (equal priority) can preempt Timer_A's timerCount++ between its read and write, so B's update is lost.
Timer_Force (higher priority) can preempt the increment between its read and write, and the write-back overwrites Force's value.
Timer_Force can run between A's increment and its check and set timerCount to 0, so the check at line 96 sees a different value.
Timer_B can preempt Timer_A after the increment and set timerCount to 1, so the check at line 96 sees B's value.
Timer_Force can preempt Timer_B between its write and its check and set timerCount to 0, so the check at line 109 fails.
Timer_A (equal priority) can preempt Timer_B and increment timerCount, so the check at line 109 no longer sees 1.
